sources.scope: Programme identity: Computer Science bachelor, English, full time, Maastricht.

Published curriculum overview: common first year, paired module choices in Year 2, elective/project semester and thesis in Year 3. The current course repository is linked but its public route did not yield a current component list.
Programme rationale and academic applications, including computing for critical sectors, cognitive robotics and software construction.
2025–26 course descriptions corroborate topic-level comparisons where they agree with the formal programme. The catalogue alone does not determine the required component list.
Faculty regulations adopted 2 June 2025, effective 1 September 2025. Articles 3.15, 4.2, 5.3 and Appendix 1 determine the illustrated route, progression and unique credits.
Career and graduate-study examples support search context only.

curriculum: The full-time English Maastricht Computer Science BSc is illustrated using the published 2025–26 regulations. Appendix 1 gives twelve four-credit courses and two six-credit projects in Year 1, ten four-credit courses and two ten-credit modules in Year 2, then six four-credit electives across Blocks 3.1 and 3.2, a six-credit Project 3-1, three four-credit courses and an 18-credit thesis. Counting each semester module and project once gives 60+60+60 EC. Appendix 1 controls formal component names and credits. Use BCS1430 Object-Oriented Modelling instead of the catalogue BCS1450 Computer Architecture and BCS2510 IT Management & Privacy instead of the catalogue year-two Operating Systems. Count Operating Systems once in year three. Year 3 ethics and computation titles follow the Appendix. The year-two modules shown are first in official order. Optional tracks, other-provider credit, the minor and exchange do not add credits to this route.
progression: A standard on-time student can meet Article 4.2 by taking the four stated foundational courses in year one and completing Project 1-2. Module 2-1 and 2-2 each require two of the four named courses and registration for or completion of at least three courses in the respective semester; Module 2-2 also requires Project 1-2. Project 3-1 requires Module 2-1 and at least three Year 3 semester-one courses registered or complete. The exam thresholds in Article 5.3 are 45 EC from Year 1 for Year 2 exams and 60 EC from Year 1 plus 40 EC from Year 2 for Year 3 exams. Thesis application additionally needs 138 EC overall, within reach after the first 150 EC. The modules include skill classes and project attendance, not counted separately. The six elective slots remain open within the formal lists and credit limits. No current-cohort rule is asserted.
components: Introduction to Computer Science (BCS1110, year 1 core course)
Objects in Programming (BCS1220, year 1 core course)
Data Structures and Algorithms (BCS1420, year 1 core course)
Introduction to Artificial Intelligence (BCS2120, year 2 core course)
Intelligent User Interfaces (BCS2130, year 2 core course)
Software Engineering and Architectures (BCS2210, year 2 core course)
Principles of Programming Languages (BCS2220, year 2 core course)
Project 3-1 (BCS3300, year 3 semester 1 project for external customers)
Year 3 electives (six 4 EC courses across Blocks 3.1 and 3.2)
Ethics and Philosophy for Computer Science
The individual thesis requires 138 EC overall, including all 60 first-year credits and at least 40 second-year credits.
